newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds snooze in quiet Friday trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds snooze in quiet Friday trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backeds fell victim to a sleepy, pre-holiday trading session.
Pass-through prices barely budged from yesterday's closing levels as current and discount coupons inched 1/32 lower.
Traders said economic data released on Friday failed to stimulate the Treasury market and the mortgage-backed market.
"We came in and the market was flat. (Gross domestic product) numbers came out and the market remained flat," a regional mortgage trader said.
"Now our market is almost unchanged across the board," he said.
The U.S. Commerce Department revised up third-quarter GDP growth by 0.1 percentage point to 2.1 percent, mostly in line with Wall Street expectations.

Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were off 1/32 at 100-10/32, yielding 117 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper was off 1/32 as well, at 100-10/32 and 100-14/32, respectively.
Traders said the next two abbreviated work weeks will keep most mortgage investors sidelined.
"There is nothing good to say except ho, ho, ho," said one trader.
